name: Full-Stack
description: A compiler, assembler, and RISC-V VM, and kernel implementation, all running in real time in your browser.

paragraphs: Full-Stack is a self-contained compiler pipeline for a small systems language (HLL). It carries source all the way to machine code and runs the result on a built-in RISC-V CPU, with every stage inspectable in a graphical IDE:

The whole toolchain is written in Rust and runs either natively (egui desktop IDE and a fsc CLI) or fully client-side in the browser via WebAssembly, VM included. The kernel target boots a real S-mode operating system on the VM: paging, processes, a filesystem, an interactive shell, a line editor, and a compiler toolchain that runs inside the VM so you can write, compile, assemble, and run a program without ever leaving the machine.
Boot the kernel target (the IDE's machine dock, or fsc run kernel.elf) and you land at a shell prompt running as pid 1:
features: A self-hosting toolchain inside the VM. Boot the kernel, drop into the shell, write

an .hll or .s file in the in-VM editor, compile it with cc, assemble it with as, link it with ld, and run the result, all without leaving the guest. The compiler (/bin/cc), assembler (/bin/as), and linker (/bin/ld) are…
A real interactive OS. An S-mode kernel with Sv39 paging, per-process address

spaces, a round-robin preemptive scheduler, an inode read-write filesystem, and a shell with pipes, redirection, background jobs, and file management. Foreground programs return to the prompt on exit and can be…
A complete front-to-back compiler. Lexer, parser, semantic analysis, typed SSA
